articles.title: US sanctions Hezbollah-linked charity in push against Iran's proxies, Treasury says
articles.description: By Andrea ShalalNov 18 (Reuters) - The United States on Wednesday issued new Hezbollah-related sanctions targeting three people based in Lebanon, and three entities as part of a broader effort to shut down Iran's proxy networks, the Treasury Department said.Treasury said its Office of Foreign Assets Control designated the Hezbollah-affiliated charity Ta’awanu Association and its founder, along with two Lebanese brothers who the US said have aided the Islamic militant group with a gold- and cash-smuggling network.

articles.title: Explainer-What is Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah militia?
articles.description: By Michael Georgy and Ahmed RasheedDUBAI/BAGHDAD Nov 18 (Reuters) - Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has made his riskiest move since he came to power six months ago: directly confronting the heavily armed Shi'ite militias that function as proxies of Iran.Zaidi has told his security forces to prepare to take onKataib Hezbollah, the most powerful Iran-aligned group, which officials have accused of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of state-owned oil.

articles.title: Iraqi leader's planned crackdown on pro-Iran militias is riskiest move yet
articles.description: By Ahmed Rasheed and Michael GeorgyBAGHDAD/DUBAI Nov 17 (Reuters) - Just six months after coming to power as a political novice, Iraq's Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi is planning his riskiest move yet: directly confronting the heavily armed Shi'ite militias that function as proxies of Iran.The 41-year-old businessman-turned-politician has told his security forces to prepare to take on Iran's most powerful ally in Iraq, Kataib Hezbollah, a group which officials have accused of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of state-owned oil.
